title: Serialized account transfers in an in-process ledger
name: Ledger transfer service

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code protects account balances from concurrent transfers? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is no defect. Both account locks are taken before the balances are read, and the read, the funds check and applyTransfer all happen while both locks are held, so no other transfer touching either account can interleave between check and write. Locks are always acquired in sorted id order, so two opposite transfers (A->B and B->A) cannot deadlock. KeyedMutex chains each waiter on the previous tail, so waiters run in FIFO order, and the map entry is removed only if no later waiter has replaced the tail. Both releases sit in finally blocks, so validation errors still free the locks. This assumes a single process owns these accounts; that is a deployment constraint, not a bug in the code shown.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two requests run at the same time: transfer A->B and transfer B->A (with A < B by string order). What happens?
choices: Both may deadlock, because each holds one account lock and waits for the other
Both acquire A's lock first, so one waits for the other to finish completely and then runs
They run fully in parallel because the locks are keyed by the source account only
The second request fails immediately with a lock error
choiceQuestions.explanation: transfer() sorts the ids into firstId/secondId before locking, so both requests lock A first. Whichever gets A first also takes B, finishes, and releases; the other then proceeds. Deadlock needs opposite acquisition order, which the sort prevents. Locks cover both accounts, not just the source, and KeyedMutex waits rather than failing.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Three transfers out of the same account call acquire() for that account in order T1, T2, T3 while T1 is still running. In what order do they enter the critical section?
choices: In arbitrary order, whichever promise resolves first
T3 first, because it holds the newest tail
T1, then T2 and T3 together
choiceQuestions.explanation: Each acquire() awaits the previous tail and installs a new tail that resolves only after its own release is called. T2 waits on T1's tail, T3 waits on T2's, giving FIFO order. Nothing lets T3 skip ahead, and T2 and T3 cannot overlap because T3's previous is T2's tail.

choiceQuestions.prompt: applyTransfer throws a database error. What state are the locks in afterwards?
choices: Both locks are released by the finally blocks and the error propagates to the caller
The second lock is released but the first stays held until the process restarts
Both locks stay held because the error escapes before release is called
The error is swallowed and the locks are released
choiceQuestions.explanation: releaseSecond() runs in the inner finally and releaseFirst() in the outer finally, so both run regardless of the error. Neither try block has a catch, so the error is rethrown to the caller rather than swallowed.
